newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei ends just below 21,000 on US election.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei ends just below 21,000 on US election.

text.p: Japan's key stock index surged to end just below 21,000 on Wednesday, relieved by Bill Clinton's re-election as U.S. president and the Republicans' retention of control in Congress. The market's next focus will be the announcement of Japan's new cabinet members, brokers said.
The Nikkei 225 average soared 399.19 points, or 1.94 percent, to finish at 20,991.52. Its December futures were 480 points higher at 21,100.
"The Republicans' keeping control of the House eased fears of possible dollar falls and pushed up the stocks," said Shigenori Okazaki, a political analyst at S.B.C. Warburg.
